title: Out-of-Order Execution Scoreboard Reservation Station
description:
### Problem statement
An out-of-order execution engine tracks instruction dependencies using a 4-entry reservation station. Each slot records `busy`, destination tag `dest_tag [1:0]`, source 1 tag `src1_tag [1:0]`, source 1 ready `src1_rdy`, source 2 tag `src2_tag [1:0]`, and source 2 ready `src2_rdy`. When an instruction issues (`issue_val=1`), it allocates the lowest free slot. When an execution unit broadcasts a completed tag (`cdb_val=1, cdb_tag [1:0]`), any slot waiting on that tag marks its corresponding source as ready. When both sources for a slot become ready (`src1_rdy && src2_rdy`), that slot asserts its dispatch readiness `rdy_mask [3:0]`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_ooo_scoreboard(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       issue_val,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_dest,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_s1,
    input  logic       issue_s1_rdy,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_s2,
    input  logic       issue_s2_rdy,
    input  logic       cdb_val,
    input  logic [1:0] cdb_tag,
    output logic [3:0] slot_busy,
    output logic [3:0] rdy_mask,
    output logic       full
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous reservation station registers across 4 slots (0..3).
- On `issue_val=1`, allocate lowest index `i` where `!slot_busy[i]`.
  - Store dest tag, s1 tag, s1 ready, s2 tag, s2 ready. Set `slot_busy[i] <= 1`.
- On `cdb_val=1`:
  - For every busy slot: if `!s1_rdy && (s1_tag == cdb_tag)`, set `s1_rdy <= 1`.
  - If `!s2_rdy && (s2_tag == cdb_tag)`, set `s2_rdy <= 1`.
- Output `rdy_mask[i] = slot_busy[i] && s1_rdy[i] && s2_rdy[i]`.
- Output `full = &slot_busy`.
- `rst_n` clears all slot busy and ready registers to 0.

#### Notes
Distributed reservation stations eliminate WAR and WAW hazards by dynamic register renaming.
starter_code:
module sv_i_ooo_scoreboard(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       issue_val,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_dest,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_s1,
    input  logic       issue_s1_rdy,
    input  logic [1:0] issue_s2,
    input  logic       issue_s2_rdy,
    input  logic       cdb_val,
    input  logic [1:0] cdb_tag,
    output logic [3:0] slot_busy,
    output logic [3:0] rdy_mask,
    output logic       full
);
    // TODO: implement 4-entry out-of-order reservation scoreboard

endmodule
solution_hints: Find the lowest unallocated slot index when issue_val is asserted.
Compare cdb_tag against pending source operands across all busy reservation slots.
A slot asserts rdy_mask when both of its source operands are resolved.

title: Network-on-Chip Router Virtual Channel Allocator
description:
### Problem statement
In an on-chip network router, incoming flits from 2 input ports (Port 0 and Port 1) each request one of 2 virtual channels (`req_vc [1:0]`) targeted at output port 0 or output port 1. When both input ports contend for the identical output virtual channel (`dest_port_p0 == dest_port_p1 && req_vc_p0 == req_vc_p1`), a round-robin priority arbiter alternates grant between Port 0 and Port 1. If their targets differ, both ports are granted simultaneously without stalls.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_vc_router(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       req_p0,
    input  logic       dest_p0,
    input  logic       vc_p0,
    input  logic       req_p1,
    input  logic       dest_p1,
    input  logic       vc_p1,
    output logic       grant_p0,
    output logic       grant_p1,
    output logic       contention_warn
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register round-robin priority pointer `p0_prio` on posedge clk.
- Conflict condition: `conflict = req_p0 && req_p1 && (dest_p0 == dest_p1) && (vc_p0 == vc_p1)`.
- Combinational grants:
  - If `conflict`:
    - If `p0_prio`: `grant_p0 = 1, grant_p1 = 0`.
    - Else: `grant_p0 = 0, grant_p1 = 1`.
  - Else: `grant_p0 = req_p0, grant_p1 = req_p1`.
- Output `contention_warn = conflict`.
- Priority pointer update on posedge clk: if `conflict`, toggle `p0_prio <= ~p0_prio`.
- `rst_n` sets `p0_prio <= 1` and clears outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Virtual channel multiplexing decouples flits and avoids credit head-of-line deadlock.
starter_code:
module sv_i_vc_router(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       req_p0,
    input  logic       dest_p0,
    input  logic       vc_p0,
    input  logic       req_p1,
    input  logic       dest_p1,
    input  logic       vc_p1,
    output logic       grant_p0,
    output logic       grant_p1,
    output logic       contention_warn
);
    // TODO: implement 2-port virtual channel contention arbiter

endmodule
solution_hints: Check both destination port and target virtual channel to identify collisions.
When collision occurs, grant based on current round-robin priority pointer.
Toggle priority bit only after a contested grant.

title: MSI Cache Coherency Snooping Protocol Controller
description:
### Problem statement
A single cache line controller implements the classic MSI coherency protocol with states `INVALID (2'd0)`, `SHARED (2'd1)`, and `MODIFIED (2'd2)`. It responds to local CPU requests (`cpu_read, cpu_write`) and bus snooping events (`bus_read, bus_write`).
- In `INVALID`: `cpu_read` transitions to `SHARED`, asserting `bus_rd_req=1`. `cpu_write` transitions to `MODIFIED`, asserting `bus_rdx_req=1`.
- In `SHARED`: `cpu_write` transitions to `MODIFIED`, asserting `bus_inv_req=1`. If snooped `bus_write`, transitions to `INVALID`.
- In `MODIFIED`: if snooped `bus_read`, writes back dirty line (`writeback=1`) and transitions to `SHARED`. If snooped `bus_write`, writes back dirty line (`writeback=1`) and transitions to `INVALID`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_msi_snoop(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       cpu_read,
    input  logic       cpu_write,
    input  logic       bus_read,
    input  logic       bus_write,
    output logic [1:0] cache_state,
    output logic       writeback,
    output logic       bus_rd_req,
    output logic       bus_rdx_req,
    output logic       bus_inv_req
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous state machine on posedge clk.
- Outputs registered on posedge clk based on state transitions.
- Priority order if simultaneous events occur: bus snoop events take precedence over local CPU requests.
- `rst_n` resets `cache_state` to `INVALID (2'd0)` and all outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Snooping cache protocols guarantee single-writer, multiple-reader invariant across shared memory multiprocessors.
starter_code:
module sv_i_msi_snoop(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       cpu_read,
    input  logic       cpu_write,
    input  logic       bus_read,
    input  logic       bus_write,
    output logic [1:0] cache_state,
    output logic       writeback,
    output logic       bus_rd_req,
    output logic       bus_rdx_req,
    output logic       bus_inv_req
);
    // TODO: implement MSI snooping cache coherency controller

endmodule
solution_hints: Implement states 0 (Invalid), 1 (Shared), and 2 (Modified).
Bus snoops on modified cache lines require asserting writeback.
Promoting from Shared to Modified requires asserting bus_inv_req.

title: Floating-Point Significand Normalizer and Rounding Stage
description:
### Problem statement
In an IEEE-754 style floating-point addition pipeline, the post-addition 10-bit unnormalized significand `sig_in [9:0]` and 4-bit biased exponent `exp_in [3:0]` must be normalized such that the leading 1 appears at bit 7. Leading zero count `lzc [2:0]` shifts the significand left and subtracts from `exp_in`. The normalized 8-bit significand is then rounded up if guard bit 0 was set and LSB is odd (Round-to-Nearest-Even). Register outputs on posedge clk.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fp_norm_round(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [9:0] sig_in,
    input  logic [3:0] exp_in,
    output logic [7:0] norm_sig,
    output logic [3:0] norm_exp,
    output logic       underflow
);
```

#### Requirements
- Determine leading zeros before bit position 7 (0..7 zeros).
- Shift significand left by `lzc`: `shifted_sig = sig_in << lzc`.
- New exponent: if `exp_in < lzc`, assert `underflow <= 1, norm_exp <= 0`; else `norm_exp <= exp_in - lzc`.
- Extract 8-bit significand `shifted_sig[9:2]`.
- Apply rounding: if `shifted_sig[1] && shifted_sig[2]`, add 1 to significand.
- Output registered `norm_sig` and `norm_exp` on posedge clk.
- `rst_n` clears outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Significand normalization and deterministic rounding prevent drift in recursive linear algebra.
starter_code:
module sv_i_fp_norm_round(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [9:0] sig_in,
    input  logic [3:0] exp_in,
    output logic [7:0] norm_sig,
    output logic [3:0] norm_exp,
    output logic       underflow
);
    // TODO: implement FP significand normalization and rounding

endmodule
solution_hints: Count leading zeros to compute how many bit positions to shift left.
Subtract shift amount from exponent and detect underflow when exponent is too small.
Apply round bit to significand LSB on posedge clk.

title: Fix: DMA Scatter-Gather Descriptor Ring Address Overwrite Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A Direct Memory Access (DMA) scatter-gather engine traverses a linked list of buffer descriptors. When fetching a descriptor (`fetch_val=1`), the next descriptor pointer `next_ptr_in [7:0]` should be saved in `cur_desc_addr` only if `eol` (end of list) is 0. If `eol=1`, `cur_desc_addr` must be retained and `ring_complete` asserted. The legacy module had a bug where it always overwrote `cur_desc_addr` even on `eol=1`, jumping to an invalid memory location.

Fix the module so `cur_desc_addr` freezes and `ring_complete` asserts when `eol=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_dma_desc_ring(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       fetch_val,
    input  logic       eol,
    input  logic [7:0] next_ptr_in,
    output logic [7:0] cur_desc_addr,
    output logic       ring_complete
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous register `cur_desc_addr` on posedge clk.
- When `fetch_val=1`:
  - If `eol==0`: `cur_desc_addr <= next_ptr_in, ring_complete <= 0`.
  - If `eol==1`: hold `cur_desc_addr`, assert `ring_complete <= 1`.
- `rst_n` resets `cur_desc_addr <= 8'h00, ring_complete <= 0`.

#### Notes
Descriptor corruption in scatter-gather DMA results in kernel panics and unauthorized memory overwrite.
solution_hints: Check eol flag when fetch_val is high.
Only update cur_desc_addr if eol is low.
Assert ring_complete and keep cur_desc_addr stable when eol is high.

title: Fix: Upstream Credit Return Missing Underflow Protection
description:
### Problem statement
A credit receiver tracks consumed credits (`credit_bank [3:0]`). When downstream consumes an item (`pop_item=1`), credit is returned to upstream by pulsing `ret_credit=1` and incrementing `credit_bank`. When upstream sends an item (`push_item=1`), `credit_bank` decrements. In the flawed implementation, the credit bank counter wrapped around past zero when push exceeded returned credits, corrupting the credit budget.

Fix the module so `credit_bank` does not underflow below 0, and accurately returns credits when items pop.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_credit_leak(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       push_item,
    input  logic       pop_item,
    output logic [3:0] credit_bank,
    output logic       ret_credit
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous register `credit_bank` initialized to 4'd8 on reset.
- On posedge clk:
  - Credit return pulse: `ret_credit <= pop_item`.
  - Balance update:
    - If `pop_item && !push_item`: `credit_bank <= (credit_bank < 15) ? credit_bank + 1 : credit_bank`.
    - If `push_item && !pop_item`: `credit_bank <= (credit_bank > 0) ? credit_bank - 1 : 0`.
    - If both or neither: `credit_bank` unchanged.
- `rst_n` sets `credit_bank <= 4'd8, ret_credit <= 0`.

#### Notes
Credit leaks in lossless network fabrics cause permanent packet stalls.
solution_hints: Initialize credit_bank to 8 on reset.
Protect against underflow by clamping credit_bank at 0.
Pulse ret_credit high on every pop_item.

title: Implement the timing: PCIe Transaction Layer Packet Framing State Engine
description:
### Problem statement
A PCI Express Transaction Layer Packet (TLP) transmitter emits framed packets with exact cycle alignment. On transmission start (`start_tlp=1` with length `payload_len [2:0]`, 1..7 dwords):
- Cycle 1: assert `sop=1` (Start of Packet), emit Header DWORD 0 (`hdr_phase=0`).
- Cycle 2: `sop=0`, emit Header DWORD 1 (`hdr_phase=1`).
- Cycle 3: emit Header DWORD 2 (`hdr_phase=2`).
- Cycle 4+: emit payload data dwords (`data_phase=1`), counting down payload length. On the last payload dword, assert `eop=1` (End of Packet).
- After `eop`, return to IDLE.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_pcie_tlp(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start_tlp,
    input  logic [2:0] payload_len,
    output logic       sop,
    output logic       eop,
    output logic       in_header,
    output logic       in_payload,
    output logic [1:0] hdr_dword
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous FSM on posedge clk.
- From IDLE on `start_tlp=1`:
  - Register payload count.
  - Transition through 3 header cycles: DWORD 0 (sop=1), DWORD 1, DWORD 2.
  - Transition to payload: count transferred dwords until payload length reached, asserting `eop=1` on terminal dword.
- `rst_n` resets FSM to IDLE, all outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Precise STP/END and framing markers ensure link-layer framing alignment across multi-lane PHYs.

module sv_i_trace_pcie_tlp(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start_tlp,
    input  logic [2:0] payload_len,

    output logic       eop,
    output logic       in_header,
    output logic       in_payload,
    output logic [1:0] hdr_dword
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Traverse header DWORDs 0, 1, and 2 before entering payload phase.
Assert sop during header DWORD 0.
Assert eop on the terminal beat of the payload phase.

title: Implement the timing: AXI4 WRAP4 Burst Address Sequence Generator
description:
### Problem statement
In ARM AMBA AXI4, a WRAP burst wraps back to the lower boundary when crossing a wrapped cache-line address threshold. For a 4-beat wrapping burst (`burst_len=4`) of 4-byte words, the 16-byte boundary aligns at `addr[3:0]`. When initial address `start_addr [7:0]` arrives with `start_burst=1`, output `beat_addr [7:0]` outputs `start_addr`. On each subsequent handshake (`next_beat=1`), `beat_addr` increments by 4 within the 16-byte boundary (`beat_addr[3:2] <= beat_addr[3:2] + 1`, wrapping 3->0). On beat 4, `last_beat` asserts.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_axi_wrap(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start_burst,
    input  logic [7:0] start_addr,
    input  logic       next_beat,
    output logic [7:0] beat_addr,
    output logic [1:0] beat_idx,
    output logic       last_beat
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous address generator on posedge clk.
- When `start_burst=1`: latch `start_addr`, set `beat_addr <= start_addr, beat_idx <= 0`.
- When `next_beat=1`:
  - `beat_idx <= beat_idx + 1`.
  - Increment word index: `beat_addr[3:2] <= beat_addr[3:2] + 1` (bits [7:4] and [1:0] remain constant).
- Output `last_beat = (beat_idx == 2'd3)`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Wrapping bursts align critical cache-line words first before fetching surrounding words.
starter_code:
module sv_i_trace_axi_wrap(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start_burst,
    input  logic [7:0] start_addr,
    input  logic       next_beat,
    output logic [7:0] beat_addr,
    output logic [1:0] beat_idx,
    output logic       last_beat
);
    // TODO: implement AXI4 4-beat wrapping burst address tracker

endmodule
solution_hints: Only increment bits [3:2] of beat_addr on each beat.
Upper bits [7:4] and byte offsets [1:0] remain invariant throughout the burst.
Assert last_beat when beat_idx equals 3.

title: Checker: Dual-Core Lockstep Instruction Trace Comparator
description:
### Problem statement
In ISO 26262 ASIL-D automotive processors, dual cores run in lockstep with Core 1 delayed by a 2-cycle stagger delay relative to Core 0 to prevent common-cause spatial faults. The lockstep comparator delays Core 0's program counter `core0_pc [7:0]` by 2 cycles through a delay line and compares it against Core 1's live PC `core1_pc [7:0]`. If they mismatch (`delayed_core0_pc != core1_pc`) on any active cycle (`val=1`), an uncorrectable fault pulse `divergence_fault` fires and latches `sticky_fault=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_lockstep_divergence(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       val,
    input  logic [7:0] core0_pc,
    input  logic [7:0] core1_pc,
    output logic       divergence_fault,
    output logic       sticky_fault
);
```

#### Requirements
- 2-stage synchronous delay registers for Core 0 PC: `d1_pc <= core0_pc`, `d2_pc <= d1_pc`.
- Synchronous comparison on posedge clk:
  - If `val && (d2_pc != core1_pc)`: `divergence_fault <= 1, sticky_fault <= 1`.
  - Else: `divergence_fault <= 0` (sticky_fault retains 1 once asserted).
- `rst_n` clears all pipeline registers, fault pulses, and sticky flags to 0.

#### Notes
Redundant lockstep execution detects soft errors and transient radiation upsets.
starter_code:
module sv_i_chk_lockstep_divergence(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       val,
    input  logic [7:0] core0_pc,
    input  logic [7:0] core1_pc,
    output logic       divergence_fault,
    output logic       sticky_fault
);
    // TODO: implement 2-cycle staggered lockstep core divergence monitor

endmodule
solution_hints: Delay core0_pc by two clock cycles through two consecutive flip-flops.
Compare the delayed Core 0 PC against core1_pc whenever val is high.
Latch sticky_fault permanently on first detected mismatch.

title: Checker: AXI-Stream Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) Overflow Guard
description:
### Problem statement
An AXI4-Stream packet checker verifies that incoming packets do not violate maximum length constraints (`max_beats [3:0]`). During active packet transfer (`tvalid && tready`), an internal beat counter counts words until `tlast=1`. If the beat count exceeds `max_beats` before `tlast` appears, the checker asserts `err_mtu_exceeded=1`. If `tlast` asserts on the very first beat when `min_beats=2` (`min_len_en=1`), `err_undersized` asserts.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_axis_trunc(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       tvalid,
    input  logic       tready,
    input  logic       tlast,
    input  logic [3:0] max_beats,
    input  logic       min_len_en,
    output logic       err_mtu_exceeded,
    output logic       err_undersized,
    output logic [3:0] beat_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `beat_cnt` on posedge clk.
- When `tvalid && tready`:
  - If `tlast`:
    - If `min_len_en && (beat_cnt == 0)`: `err_undersized <= 1`.
    - Else: `err_undersized <= 0`.
    - `beat_cnt <= 0`.
  - Else:
    - `err_undersized <= 0`.
    - If `beat_cnt >= max_beats`: `err_mtu_exceeded <= 1`.
    - Else: `err_mtu_exceeded <= 0`.
    - `beat_cnt <= beat_cnt + 1`.
- `rst_n` clears all counts and error flags to 0.

#### Notes
Detecting packet length violations prevents downstream buffer overflows and DMA descriptor overrun.
starter_code:
module sv_i_chk_axis_trunc(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       tvalid,
    input  logic       tready,
    input  logic       tlast,
    input  logic [3:0] max_beats,
    input  logic       min_len_en,
    output logic       err_mtu_exceeded,
    output logic       err_undersized,
    output logic [3:0] beat_cnt
);
    // TODO: implement AXI-Stream packet MTU and undersized checker

endmodule
solution_hints: Count beats on each successful handshake (tvalid && tready).
Assert err_undersized if tlast asserts when beat_cnt is 0 and min_len_en is high.
Assert err_mtu_exceeded when beat_cnt exceeds max_beats before tlast.

title: Hardware Ticket Lock Fair Mutual Exclusion Synchronizer
description:
### Problem statement
A hardware ticket lock guarantees first-come first-served mutual exclusion among 4 processor cores. The lock maintains a `next_ticket [3:0]` and a `now_serving [3:0]` counter. When a core requests a lock (`req[i]=1`), it receives a unique ticket number from `next_ticket`, and `next_ticket` increments. A core holds the lock (`lock_granted[i]=1`) when its allocated ticket equals `now_serving`. When the holding core releases the lock (`release=1`), `now_serving` increments, granting the lock to the next waiting core.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_ticket_lock(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    input  logic       release_lock,
    output logic [3:0] lock_granted,
    output logic [3:0] now_serving,
    output logic [3:0] next_ticket
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `now_serving` and `next_ticket` on posedge clk, both initialized to 0.
- Up to 1 core can request per cycle (lowest active bit of `req` allocated if multiple).
- When core `i` requests and is not already holding a ticket:
  - Core `i` records its ticket = `next_ticket`.
  - `next_ticket <= next_ticket + 1`.
- Output `lock_granted[i] = (ticket[i] == now_serving) && core_waiting[i]`.
- When `release_lock=1`: `now_serving <= now_serving + 1`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Ticket locks prevent CPU starvation and guarantee bounded acquisition latency in NUMA architectures.
starter_code:
module sv_i_ticket_lock(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    input  logic       release_lock,
    output logic [3:0] lock_granted,
    output logic [3:0] now_serving,
    output logic [3:0] next_ticket
);
    // TODO: implement hardware ticket lock mutual exclusion engine

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain separate next_ticket and now_serving counters.
Record each core's assigned ticket in an internal register array.
Assert lock_granted for core i when its ticket matches now_serving.

title: Radix-4 Booth Multiplier Partial Product Generator
description:
### Problem statement
A Radix-4 Booth recoder examines a 3-bit window `{y[2*i+1], y[2*i], y[2*i-1]}` of multiplier operand $Y$ and multiplicand $X$ (`m_in [7:0]`) to generate a partial product `pp_out [9:0]` and add/sub sign `sub_neg`:
- 3'b000 or 3'b111: factor 0
- 3'b001 or 3'b010: factor +1 (pp = $X$)
- 3'b011: factor +2 (pp = $2X$)
- 3'b100: factor -2 (pp = $2X$, sub_neg=1)
- 3'b101 or 3'b110: factor -1 (pp = $X$, sub_neg=1)
Output `pp_out` is computed combinational and registered on posedge clk.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_booth_radix4(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [2:0] booth_window,
    input  logic [7:0] m_in,
    output logic [9:0] pp_out,
    output logic       sub_neg
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered outputs on posedge clk.
- Booth decoding:
  - Window 0 or 7: `pp_out <= 0, sub_neg <= 0`.
  - Window 1 or 2: `pp_out <= {2'b00, m_in}, sub_neg <= 0`.
  - Window 3: `pp_out <= {1'b0, m_in, 1'b0}, sub_neg <= 0`.
  - Window 4: `pp_out <= {1'b0, m_in, 1'b0}, sub_neg <= 1`.
  - Window 5 or 6: `pp_out <= {2'b00, m_in}, sub_neg <= 1`.
- `rst_n` clears outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Radix-4 Booth recoding halves the required number of partial product additions in high-speed multipliers.
solution_hints: Decode the 3-bit window to determine whether factor is 0, 1, or 2.
Assert sub_neg when the window indicates a negative partial product (patterns 4, 5, 6).
Left-shift multiplicand by 1 bit to compute the 2X product.

title: AES MixColumns Matrix Transformation Column Processor
description:
### Problem statement
In the AES encryption round, each 4-byte column $s = [s_0, s_1, s_2, s_3]$ undergoes the MixColumns linear transformation over $\text{GF}(2^8)$:
- $r_0 = (2 \cdot s_0) \oplus (3 \cdot s_1) \oplus s_2 \oplus s_3$
- $r_1 = s_0 \oplus (2 \cdot s_1) \oplus (3 \cdot s_2) \oplus s_3$
- $r_2 = s_0 \oplus s_1 \oplus (2 \cdot s_2) \oplus (3 \cdot s_3$
- $r_3 = (3 \cdot s_0) \oplus s_1 \oplus s_2 \oplus (2 \cdot s_3)$
where $2 \cdot x = \text{xtimes}(x)$ and $3 \cdot x = \text{xtimes}(x) \oplus x$. Register output column on posedge clk.

#### Module interface

```systemverilog
    output logic [7:0] r2,
    output logic [7:0] r3
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure GF(256) xtimes function: `xt(b) = (b[7]) ? ((b << 1) ^ 8'h1b) : (b << 1)`.
- $3 \cdot b = \text{xt}(b) \oplus b$.
- Register all 4 transformed outputs `r0..r3` on posedge clk.
- `rst_n` clears outputs to 0.

title: Fix: Multi-Bank SRAM Collision Arbiter Target Bank Decoding
description:
### Problem statement
A 2-master memory arbiter accesses 2 SRAM banks (`bank0` and `bank1`). Master 0 targets `dest0` (0: bank0, 1: bank1) and Master 1 targets `dest1`. If both masters request concurrently (`req0 && req1`):
- If `dest0 != dest1`: both masters granted (`grant0=1, grant1=1`).
- If `dest0 == dest1`: Master 0 receives priority (`grant0=1, grant1=0`).
The original author erroneously wrote `grant1 = req1 && (dest0 == dest1)` instead of `dest0 != dest1`, granting Master 1 precisely when it collided with Master 0.

Fix the module so Master 1 is granted when free of conflict with Master 0.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_sram_bank_arb(
    input  logic req0,
    input  logic dest0,
    input  logic req1,
    input  logic dest1,
    output logic grant0,
    output logic grant1,
    output logic conflict
);
```

#### Requirements
- Combinational logic.
- `grant0 = req0`.
- `conflict = req0 && req1 && (dest0 == dest1)`.
- `grant1 = req1 && (!req0 || (dest0 != dest1))`.

#### Notes
Detecting bank collisions in interleaved memories prevents silent dual-port data overwrites.
solution_hints: Master 0 receives grant whenever req0 is high.
Conflict occurs when both masters request the identical bank.
Master 1 is granted if req1 is high and there is no conflict.

title: Fix: Elastic Skid Buffer Ready Release Timing Hazard
description:
### Problem statement
A registered skid buffer decouples timing paths between upstream (`s_valid, s_ready`) and downstream (`m_valid, m_ready`). When downstream stalls (`m_ready=0`) while data is in transit, the buffer captures the word in a secondary skid register and deasserts `s_ready=0`. When downstream becomes ready (`m_ready=1`), `s_ready` must immediately reassert. In the original module, `s_ready` remained stuck low for an extra cycle, throttling pipeline throughput by 50%.

Fix the module so `s_ready` reasserts immediately when the skid register empties or downstream asserts `m_ready`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_skid_flag_glitch(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic s_valid,
    output logic s_ready,
    output logic m_valid,
    input  logic m_ready
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous state machine with skid register.
- State 0 (Empty): `s_ready = 1, m_valid = 0`.
- State 1 (Busy): `s_ready = 1, m_valid = 1`. If `s_valid && !m_ready`, go to State 2 (Skid).
- State 2 (Skid): `s_ready = 0, m_valid = 1`. If `m_ready`, transition back to State 1.
- `rst_n` clears state to 0.

#### Notes
Zero-bubble skid buffers achieve 100% sustained throughput even across stalling backpressure interfaces.
solution_hints: When in State 2 (SKID) and m_ready asserts, transition to State 1 (BUSY) instead of State 0.
s_ready is high when the buffer is not in State 2.
m_valid is high whenever the buffer contains at least one item.

title: Implement the timing: DDR3 Memory Write DQS Strobe Preamble Engine
description:
### Problem statement
In DDR3 SDRAM write bursts, the bidirectional data strobe `dqs` must follow strict JEDEC timing:
1. IDLE: High-Z / inactive (`dqs_oe=0, dqs_val=0`).
2. PREAMBLE: 1 full clock cycle driving low before data (`dqs_oe=1, dqs_val=0`).
3. TOGGLE: toggles for 4 clock cycles (8 half-cycle beats) while `dqs_oe=1`.
4. POSTAMBLE: 1 cycle driving low (`dqs_oe=1, dqs_val=0`).
5. Return to IDLE.
When write trigger `start_write=1` asserts, generate the cycle-by-cycle strobe control signals.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_ddr3_dqs(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic start_write,
    output logic dqs_oe,
    output logic dqs_val,
    output logic [2:0] burst_step,
    output logic in_burst
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous FSM tracking PREAMBLE (step 0), TOGGLE (steps 1..4), and POSTAMBLE (step 5).
- When `start_write=1`: transition to PREAMBLE, `dqs_oe <= 1, dqs_val <= 0, burst_step <= 0, in_burst <= 1`.
- During TOGGLE (steps 1..4): toggle `dqs_val <= ~dqs_val` each clock cycle, `burst_step <= burst_step + 1`.
- During POSTAMBLE (step 5): `dqs_oe <= 1, dqs_val <= 0`.
- Next cycle: `dqs_oe <= 0, in_burst <= 0, burst_step <= 0` (IDLE).
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Precise preamble timing gives receiver differential amplifiers time to settle before burst data arrives.

title: Implement the timing: Gigabit Ethernet Inter-Frame Gap Enforcer
description:
### Problem statement
IEEE 802.3 Gigabit Ethernet standard dictates a mandatory minimum 12-octet Inter-Frame Gap (IFG) of 12 idle clock cycles (`tx_en=0`) between successive transmitted frames. After packet transmission ends (`tx_last=1` with `tx_val=1`), an IFG timer counts 12 clock cycles. Output `tx_ready` must remain low during these 12 cycles, and assert high on the 13th cycle to permit the next packet frame.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_gmii_ifg(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tx_val,
    input  logic tx_last,
    output logic tx_ready,
    output logic [3:0] ifg_timer
);
```

#### Requirements
- In IDLE: `tx_ready = 1, ifg_timer = 0`.
- When transmitting: `tx_ready = 1`.
- When `tx_val && tx_last`:
  - Deassert `tx_ready <= 0`.
  - Count `ifg_timer` from 1 to 12 on successive clock cycles.
  - When `ifg_timer == 12`: reassert `tx_ready <= 1, ifg_timer <= 0`.
- `rst_n` sets `tx_ready <= 1, ifg_timer <= 0`.

#### Notes
IFG gives Ethernet receivers time to recover carrier sync and prepare DMA buffer descriptors.
solution_hints: Deassert tx_ready immediately upon seeing tx_val and tx_last.
Count 12 idle cycles in ifg_timer.
Reassert tx_ready when the 12th cycle concludes.

title: Branch Target Buffer with Two-Bit Saturating Predictor
description:

A 4-entry direct-mapped Branch Target Buffer (BTB) indexed by PC bits `[1:0]` predicts branch outcomes. Each entry stores valid bit `v`, tag `pc_tag [3:0]`, target address `target [7:0]`, and a 2-bit saturating counter `state [1:0]` (2'b00: Strong Not-Taken, 2'b01: Weak Not-Taken, 2'b10: Weak Taken, 2'b11: Strong Taken). title: Weighted Fair Queuing Virtual Finish Time Generator
description:
### Problem statement
A Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ) scheduler assigns virtual finish tags $F_i$ to arriving packets: $F_i = \max(V, F_{i-1}) + \frac{L}{\text{weight}}$, where $V$ is global virtual time and $L$ is packet length. In this dual-queue engine, Queue 0 has weight 1 (increment $L$) and Queue 1 has weight 2 (increment $L >> 1$). Global virtual time $V$ increments whenever a packet departs. Given incoming packet length `pkt_len [5:0]`, target queue `q_sel`, and arrival pulse `arrival`, compute and register the assigned virtual finish tag `finish_tag [7:0]`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       arrival,
    input  logic       q_sel,
    input  logic [5:0] pkt_len,
    input  logic       depart,
    output logic [7:0] finish_tag,
    output logic [7:0] global_vt
);
```

- Synchronous registers: `v_time` (global virtual time), `last_f0`, `last_f1`.
- When `depart=1`: `v_time <= v_time + 1`.
- When `arrival=1` on posedge clk:
  - Queue 0: `base = (v_time > last_f0) ? v_time : last_f0`; `f_new = base + pkt_len`.
    - Update `last_f0 <= f_new, finish_tag <= f_new`.
  - Queue 1: `base = (v_time > last_f1) ? v_time : last_f1`; `f_new = base + (pkt_len >> 1)`.
    - Update `last_f1 <= f_new, finish_tag <= f_new`.
- Output `global_vt = v_time`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
WFQ virtual finish times provide delay and bandwidth guarantees proportional to assigned weights.

title: Montgomery Modular Multiplier Word Processing Step
description:
### Problem statement
In RSA/ECC hardware accelerators, Montgomery multiplication computes $S_{i+1} = (S_i + a_i \cdot B + q_i \cdot M) / 2$, where quotient bit $q_i = (S_{i,0} \oplus (a_i \cdot B_0)) \pmod 2$. This operation avoids costly hardware divisions by making the lowest bit of the sum zero so it can be cleanly shifted right by 1 bit. Given current accumulator $S$ (`acc_in [8:0]`), operand $B$ (`b_in [7:0]`), modulus $M$ (`m_in [7:0]`, odd), and multiplier bit `a_bit`, compute and register the next accumulator value `acc_out [8:0]`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [8:0] acc_in,
    input  logic [7:0] b_in,
    input  logic [7:0] m_in,
    input  logic       a_bit,
    output logic [8:0] acc_out,
    output logic       q_bit
);
```

#### Requirements
- Combinational intermediate calculation:
  - `q = acc_in[0] ^ (a_bit & b_in[0])`.
  - `term_b = a_bit ? {1'b0, b_in} : 9'd0`.
  - `term_m = q ? {1'b0, m_in} : 9'd0`.
  - `sum = acc_in + term_b + term_m`.
  - Next accumulator: `next_acc = sum[9:1]` (sum[0] is guaranteed 0).
- Synchronous registered outputs `acc_out <= next_acc` and `q_bit <= q` on posedge clk.
- `rst_n` clears outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Montgomery reduction replaces trial division by modular shifts in public-key cryptography.

title: Fix: Four-Bit Gray-to-Binary Pointer Decoder Incomplete XOR Chain
description:
### Problem statement
In an asynchronous FIFO read domain, the synchronized write pointer in Gray code `gray_in [3:0]` must be converted back to binary `bin_out [3:0]` to compute occupancy. The standard 4-bit Gray-to-binary conversion is:
- `bin[3] = gray[3]`
- `bin[2] = bin[3] ^ gray[2]`
- `bin[1] = bin[2] ^ gray[1]`
- `bin[0] = bin[1] ^ gray[0]`
The designer made a bug in the XOR chain by calculating `bin[0] = gray[1] ^ gray[0]` instead of cascading `bin[1] ^ gray[0]`, producing incorrect binary counts for upper-half Gray codes.

Fix the module so `bin_out` performs full cascading Gray-to-binary reconstruction.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_fifo_gray_bin(
    input  logic [3:0] gray_in,
    output logic [3:0] bin_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- `bin_out[3] = gray_in[3]`.
- `bin_out[2] = bin_out[3] ^ gray_in[2]`.
- `bin_out[1] = bin_out[2] ^ gray_in[1]`.
- `bin_out[0] = bin_out[1] ^ gray_in[0]`.

#### Notes
Accurate Gray-to-binary conversion in CDC logic prevents false full/empty flag evaluations.
solution_hints: bin_out[3] is equal to gray_in[3].
Each subsequent lower bit is the XOR of the preceding calculated binary bit with the current Gray bit.
Make sure bin_out[0] uses bin_out[1] ^ gray_in[0].

title: Fix: Non-Restoring Divider Quotient Bit Assignment Polarity
description:
### Problem statement
In a non-restoring sequential divider stage, when trial remainder `rem_diff` is non-negative (`rem_diff[4] == 0`), the new quotient bit is 1. If trial remainder is negative (`rem_diff[4] == 1`), the quotient bit is 0. The legacy module had inverted the quotient bit polarity, writing `q_bit = rem_diff[4]`, resulting in a bitwise-inverted quotient.

Fix the module so `q_bit` is assigned 1 when remainder difference is non-negative, and 0 when negative.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_div_quotient_bit(
    input  logic [4:0] rem_diff,
    output logic       q_bit
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- `q_bit = ~rem_diff[4]`.

#### Notes
Sign-bit misinterpretations in non-restoring dividers lead to inverse quotient results.
solution_hints: Check the MSB rem_diff[4] representing the sign.
A zero sign indicates a non-negative difference, yielding quotient bit 1.
Invert the sign bit to produce q_bit.

title: Implement the timing: I2C Repeated-Start and Slave Clock Stretching State Machine
description:
### Problem statement
An I2C bus master controller supports Repeated-START (`rep_start`) and responds to slave clock stretching (`scl_in=0`). In normal operation, SCL cycles high for 1 cycle and low for 1 cycle. When `rep_start=1` arrives while SCL is high, the master pulls SDA low (`sda_out=0`) while SCL remains high to create the START condition. When a slave holds SCL low (`scl_in=0`), the master enters STRETCH state, holding all operations and freezing the bit timer until the slave releases SCL (`scl_in=1`).

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_i2c_rep_start(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic rep_start_req,
    input  logic scl_in,
    output logic scl_out,
    output logic sda_out,
    output logic stretching,
    output logic [1:0] i2c_state
);
```

#### Requirements
- States (0: IDLE, 1: SCL_LOW, 2: SCL_HIGH, 3: REP_START).
- If in SCL_LOW: drive `scl_out=0`. Next cycle check `scl_in`: if `scl_in==0`, `stretching <= 1`, stay in SCL_LOW; if `scl_in==1`, `stretching <= 0`, transition to SCL_HIGH.
- In SCL_HIGH: drive `scl_out=1`. If `rep_start_req`: transition to REP_START, `sda_out <= 0`.
- In REP_START: drive `scl_out=0, sda_out <= 0`, transition to SCL_LOW.
- `rst_n` resets to IDLE, `scl_out <= 1, sda_out <= 1, stretching <= 0`.

#### Notes
Clock stretching allows slow I2C peripherals to pause high-speed bus masters.

    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic rep_start_req,
    input  logic scl_in,

    output logic sda_out,
    output logic stretching,
    output logic [1:0] i2c_state
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Monitor scl_in when attempting to release SCL high.
Assert stretching and hold state when scl_in remains low.
Drive sda_out low while SCL is high to initiate repeated start.

title: Implement the timing: CAN Controller Five-Consecutive-Bit Stuffing Rule
description:
### Problem statement
In CAN bus protocol framing, NRZ coding requires that whenever 5 consecutive bits of identical polarity (all 1s or all 0s) appear in the outgoing bitstream, the transmitter must automatically stuff a single bit of opposite polarity into the transmit stream before continuing. On each clock cycle with `tx_en=1`, bit `raw_bit` arrives. If 5 consecutive identical bits occur, the transmitter halts consumption of `raw_bit` (`hold_req=1`), sets `stuffed_bit=1`, and transmits the opposite bit `tx_out = ~prev_bit`. On normal cycles, `hold_req=0, stuffed_bit=0, tx_out = raw_bit`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_can_bit_stuff(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tx_en,
    input  logic raw_bit,
    output logic tx_out,
    output logic stuffed_bit,
    output logic hold_req,
    output logic [2:0] same_bit_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous controller on posedge clk.
- Counter `same_bit_cnt` tracks consecutive identical transmitted bits (1..5).
- If `same_bit_cnt == 5`:
  - `hold_req <= 1, stuffed_bit <= 1, tx_out <= ~last_bit`.
  - `same_bit_cnt <= 1` (the stuffed bit counts as 1).
- Else if `tx_en`:
  - `hold_req <= 0, stuffed_bit <= 0, tx_out <= raw_bit`.
  - If `raw_bit == last_bit`: `same_bit_cnt <= same_bit_cnt + 1`.
  - Else: `same_bit_cnt <= 1`.
- `rst_n` resets `same_bit_cnt <= 0, tx_out <= 1, stuffed_bit <= 0, hold_req <= 0`.

#### Notes
Bit stuffing guarantees sufficient edge transitions for receiver clock synchronization.

    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tx_en,
    input  logic raw_bit,
    output logic tx_out,
    output logic stuffed_bit,
    output logic hold_req,
    output logic [2:0] same_bit_cnt
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Track the run-length of identical bits in same_bit_cnt.
When same_bit_cnt reaches 5, insert an inverted bit.
Assert hold_req to pause the input bitstream during the stuffed cycle.

title: Checker: DRAM Open-Page Bank State Violation Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
A DRAM bank state checker monitors command sequencing on Bank 0. Commands are encoded as `cmd [1:0]` (0: NOP, 1: ACTIVATE with `row_addr [3:0]`, 2: READ/WRITE, 3: PRECHARGE). The bank starts `CLOSED`. When ACTIVATE arrives, the bank becomes `OPEN` with the opened row recorded in `open_row`. Violations:
- `err_read_when_closed`: READ/WRITE command arrives while bank is CLOSED.
- `err_activate_when_open`: ACTIVATE arrives while bank is already OPEN.
- `err_precharge_when_closed`: PRECHARGE arrives while bank is already CLOSED.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_dram_row_conflict(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [1:0] cmd,
    input  logic [3:0] row_addr,
    output logic       bank_is_open,
    output logic [3:0] open_row,
    output logic       err_read_when_closed,
    output logic       err_activate_when_open,
    output logic       err_precharge_when_closed
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous state machine on posedge clk.
- Outputs registered on posedge clk:
  - If `cmd==1` (ACT):
    - If `bank_is_open`: `err_activate_when_open <= 1`.
    - Else: `bank_is_open <= 1, open_row <= row_addr, err_activate_when_open <= 0`.
  - If `cmd==2` (READ/WRITE):
    - If `!bank_is_open`: `err_read_when_closed <= 1`.
    - Else: `err_read_when_closed <= 0`.
  - If `cmd==3` (PRE):
    - If `!bank_is_open`: `err_precharge_when_closed <= 1`.
    - Else: `bank_is_open <= 0, open_row <= 0, err_precharge_when_closed <= 0`.
- Reset sets `bank_is_open <= 0, open_row <= 0` and clears error flags to 0.

#### Notes
Detecting out-of-order DRAM commands catches memory controller state bugs before PHY corruption occurs.

    input  logic       rst_n,

    input  logic [3:0] row_addr,

    output logic [3:0] open_row,
    output logic       err_read_when_closed,
    output logic       err_activate_when_open,
    output logic       err_precharge_when_closed
);

endmodule

Assert err_read_when_closed if read arrives when bank_is_open is low.
Assert err_activate_when_open if activate arrives when bank_is_open is already high.

title: Checker: Cache Coherency Invalid-Dirty State Invariant Trap
description:
### Problem statement
In a coherent cache controller, a fundamental safety invariant states: *A cache line must NEVER be dirty (`dirty=1`) when its state is INVALID (`state == 2'b00`)*. A line marked dirty while invalid represents data that was modified locally but whose identity has been severed, resulting in irreversible silent data loss. An inline safety monitor evaluates `cache_val` (valid bit), `cache_dirty`, and `cache_state [1:0]`. If `(!cache_val || cache_state == 2'd0) && cache_dirty`, output `fatal_invariant_fault` pulses high and latches `sticky_fault=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_cache_dirty_inv(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       cache_val,
    input  logic       cache_dirty,
    input  logic [1:0] cache_state,
    output logic       fatal_invariant_fault,
    output logic       sticky_fault
);
```

#### Requirements
- Invariant violation: `violation = cache_dirty && (!cache_val || (cache_state == 2'd0))`.
- Synchronous registered outputs on posedge clk:
  - `fatal_invariant_fault <= violation`.
  - If `violation`: `sticky_fault <= 1`.
- `rst_n` clears all fault flags to 0.

#### Notes
Invariant assertion traps catch coherency race conditions during verification.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       cache_val,
    input  logic       cache_dirty,
    input  logic [1:0] cache_state,
    output logic       fatal_invariant_fault,
    output logic       sticky_fault
);
    // TODO: implement cache dirty-invalid safety invariant checker

endmodule

Assert fatal_invariant_fault on the cycle following the detected violation.
Latch sticky_fault permanently until asynchronous reset.

title: CORDIC Vectoring Mode Cartesian-to-Polar Coordinate Converter
description:
### Problem statement
In CORDIC vectoring mode, an input coordinate vector $(x_0, y_0)$ is iteratively rotated towards the positive X-axis until $y \approx 0$. At each step $i$ with elementary angle $\theta_i$ (`lut_angle [7:0]`) and shift $i$ (`shift [2:0]`):
- Direction $d_i = (y_i[7] == 1)$ ? 1 (counter-clockwise, if $y < 0$) : 0 (clockwise, if $y \ge 0$).
- If $d_i=0$ ($y \ge 0$): $x_{i+1} = x_i + (y_i >> i)$, $y_{i+1} = y_i - (x_i >> i)$, $z_{i+1} = z_i + \theta_i$.
- If $d_i=1$ ($y < 0$): $x_{i+1} = x_i - (y_i >> i)$, $y_{i+1} = y_i + (x_i >> i)$, $z_{i+1} = z_i - \theta_i$.
Register outputs on posedge clk.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_cordic_vectoring(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [2:0] shift,
    input  logic [7:0] lut_angle,
    input  logic [7:0] x_in,
    input  logic [7:0] y_in,
    input  logic [7:0] z_in,
    output logic [7:0] x_out,
    output logic [7:0] y_out,
    output logic [7:0] z_out,
    output logic       dir_taken
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous pipeline stage on posedge clk.
- Intermediate terms: `x_sh = x_in >> shift`, `y_sh = y_in >> shift`.
- If `y_in[7] == 0` (non-negative): `dir = 0, x_out <= x_in + y_sh, y_out <= y_in - x_sh, z_out <= z_in + lut_angle`.
- If `y_in[7] == 1` (negative): `dir = 1, x_out <= x_in - y_sh, y_out <= y_in + x_sh, z_out <= z_in - lut_angle`.
- Output `dir_taken <= dir`.
- `rst_n` clears all outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Vectoring CORDIC computes magnitude $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and phase angle without multipliers or square roots.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [2:0] shift,
    input  logic [7:0] lut_angle,
    input  logic [7:0] x_in,
    input  logic [7:0] y_in,
    input  logic [7:0] z_in,
    output logic [7:0] x_out,
    output logic [7:0] y_out,
    output logic [7:0] z_out,
    output logic       dir_taken
);

endmodule

If y is non-negative, rotate clockwise to decrease y.
If y is negative, rotate counter-clockwise to increase y.

title: Two-Level Adaptive Gshare Branch Predictor with Global History
description:
### Problem statement
A Gshare branch predictor indices a Pattern History Table (PHT) of 16 two-bit saturating counters using the XOR of branch address `pc [3:0]` and a 4-bit Global History Register (`ghr [3:0]`). Prediction index is `pht_idx = pc ^ ghr`. When predicting, `pred_taken = pht[pht_idx][1]`. When actual branch outcome resolves (`update_val=1` with `actual_taken`), the addressed counter increments on taken (saturating at 3) or decrements on not-taken (saturating at 0), and `ghr` shifts left: `ghr <= {ghr[2:0], actual_taken}`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_gshare_predictor(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] pc,
    input  logic       update_val,
    input  logic [3:0] update_pc,
    input  logic       actual_taken,
    output logic       pred_taken,
    output logic [3:0] cur_ghr
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `ghr` (4-bit) and 16 2-bit counters initialized to 2'b01 on reset.
- Combinational prediction: `pred_idx = pc ^ ghr`; `pred_taken = pht[pred_idx][1]`.
- Synchronous update on posedge clk:
  - If `update_val`:
    - `u_idx = update_pc ^ ghr`.
    - If `actual_taken` and `pht[u_idx] < 3`: `pht[u_idx] <= pht[u_idx] + 1`.
    - If `!actual_taken` and `pht[u_idx] > 0`: `pht[u_idx] <= pht[u_idx] - 1`.
    - `ghr <= {ghr[2:0], actual_taken}`.
- Output `cur_ghr = ghr`.
- `rst_n` sets `ghr <= 0` and all 16 counters to `2'b01`.

#### Notes
XORing global history with program counter bits prevents aliasing in correlated loops.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] pc,
    input  logic       update_val,
    input  logic [3:0] update_pc,
    input  logic       actual_taken,
    output logic       pred_taken,
    output logic [3:0] cur_ghr
);

Check MSB of the 2-bit counter for prediction.
Shift actual_taken into ghr on each update.

title: Time-Division Multiplexed (TDM) Four-Channel Audio Framer
description:
### Problem statement
A Time-Division Multiplexed (TDM) digital audio interface transmits 4 multiplexed 8-bit audio channels (Channel 0..3) over a single serial data wire `sdata`. A frame consists of 32 bit periods. Frame sync `fsync` pulses high for 1 clock cycle during the first bit of Channel 0 (bit 0). During each channel slot (8 bits), the channel byte `ch0..ch3 [7:0]` is serialized MSB first (`sdata <= ch[7-bit]`). Channels are latched into internal shift registers at the start of each frame.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog

    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       load_frame,
    input  logic [7:0] ch0,

    input  logic [7:0] ch3,
    output logic       sdata,
    output logic       fsync,
    output logic [1:0] cur_channel,

);
```

- Active channel: `cur_channel = bit_cnt[4:3]`.
- Frame sync: `fsync = (bit_cnt == 5'd0)`.
- When `bit_cnt == 0` and `load_frame=1`: latch channels into internal 32-bit shift register `{ch0, ch1, ch2, ch3}`.
- Serial data: `sdata <= shift_reg[31]`.
- Shift left each cycle: `shift_reg <= {shift_reg[30:0], 1'b0}`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
TDM interfaces aggregate multichannel surround audio without multiplying serial PCB traces.

title: Starvation-Free Priority Arbiter with Age Promotion Threshold
description:
### Problem statement
A dual-requester arbiter services High-Priority Master 0 (`req0`) and Low-Priority Master 1 (`req1`). Normally, Master 0 is granted whenever requested. However, if Master 1 is starved waiting for more than `age_limit [2:0]` cycles while `req1=1` and `grant1=0`, Master 1 is promoted to urgent status (`promoted=1`) and takes absolute priority over Master 0 until granted.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_prio_age_arbiter(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       req0,
    input  logic       req1,
    input  logic [2:0] age_limit,
    output logic       grant0,
    output logic       grant1,
    output logic       promoted,
    output logic [2:0] m1_age
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous age counter `m1_age` on posedge clk.
- If `req1 && !grant1`: increment `m1_age` (cap at 7).
- If `grant1 || !req1`: reset `m1_age <= 0`.
- Output `promoted = req1 && (m1_age >= age_limit)`.
- Combinational grant logic:
  - If `promoted`: `grant1 = 1, grant0 = 0`.
  - Else if `req0`: `grant0 = 1, grant1 = 0`.
  - Else if `req1`: `grant0 = 0, grant1 = 1`.
  - Else: `grant0 = 0, grant1 = 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Dynamic age promotion guarantees worst-case wait bounds while retaining high average priority bias.

title: Fix: Square Root Accumulator Post-Correction Restoration Bug
description:
### Problem statement
In an iterative restoring square root datapath, when a trial subtraction produces a negative remainder (`trial_diff[5] == 1`), the accumulator must restore its previous positive value `prev_acc` rather than retaining the negative difference. The legacy designer failed to implement this multiplexer, storing `trial_diff` unconditionally and corrupting both the remainder and subsequent root bits.

Fix the module so `acc_out` restores `prev_acc` when `trial_diff` is negative, and loads `trial_diff` when non-negative.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_sqrt_rem_sign(
    input  logic [4:0] prev_acc,
    input  logic [5:0] trial_diff,
    output logic [4:0] acc_out,
    output logic       trial_success
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- `trial_success = ~trial_diff[5]`.
- `acc_out = trial_success ? trial_diff[4:0] : prev_acc`.

#### Notes
Restoring steps ensure non-negative partial remainders across iterative root extractions.
solution_hints: Check trial_diff[5] to detect negative differences.
Set trial_success high when difference is non-negative.
Select trial_diff[4:0] on success, or restore prev_acc on failure.

title: Fix: Floating-Point Exponent Subtraction Underflow Clamping
description:
### Problem statement
When normalizing a floating-point significand by shifting left by `shift_cnt [2:0]`, the exponent `exp_in [3:0]` must be decremented: `exp_out = exp_in - shift_cnt`. If `shift_cnt > exp_in`, an underflow occurs: `exp_out` must be clamped to 0, and `underflow_flag` asserted. The original designer used a simple unsigned subtraction without clamping, causing underflow to roll over to large numbers (e.g., 2 - 3 = 15).

Fix the module so `exp_out` clamps to 4'd0 and asserts `underflow_flag` whenever `shift_cnt > exp_in`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_fp_underflow_clamp(
    input  logic [3:0] exp_in,
    input  logic [2:0] shift_cnt,
    output logic [3:0] exp_out,
    output logic       underflow_flag
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- If `shift_cnt > exp_in`: `exp_out = 4'd0, underflow_flag = 1'b1`.
- Else: `exp_out = exp_in - shift_cnt, underflow_flag = 1'b0`.

#### Notes
Clamping underflowing exponents to zero is required for IEEE-754 subnormal/denormal handling.
solution_hints: Compare shift_cnt against exp_in.
When shift_cnt is strictly greater than exp_in, clamp exp_out to 0.
Assert underflow_flag on underflow.

title: Implement the timing: IEEE 1149.1 JTAG TAP Controller State Engine
description:
### Problem statement
An IEEE 1149.1 Test Access Port (TAP) state machine transitions among 16 states based on Test Mode Select `tms` on posedge clk. Key states:
- 4'h0: TEST_LOGIC_RESET
- 4'h1: RUN_TEST_IDLE
- 4'h2: SELECT_DR_SCAN
- 4'h3: CAPTURE_DR
- 4'h4: SHIFT_DR
- 4'h5: EXIT1_DR
- 4'h6: PAUSE_DR
- 4'h7: EXIT2_DR
- 4'h8: UPDATE_DR
From RESET: if `tms=0`, transition to RUN_TEST_IDLE (4'h1). If `tms=1`, stay in RESET.
From RUN_TEST_IDLE: if `tms=1`, go to SELECT_DR_SCAN (4'h2); if `tms=0`, stay in IDLE.
From SELECT_DR_SCAN: if `tms=0`, go to CAPTURE_DR (4'h3); if `tms=1`, go to SELECT_IR_SCAN (4'h9).
From CAPTURE_DR: if `tms=0`, go to SHIFT_DR (4'h4); if `tms=1`, go to EXIT1_DR (4'h5).
From SHIFT_DR: if `tms=0`, stay in SHIFT_DR; if `tms=1`, go to EXIT1_DR.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_jtag_tap(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tms,
    output logic [3:0] tap_state,
    output logic in_shift_dr,
    output logic in_run_idle
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 16-state TAP machine on posedge clk.
- Output flags:
  - `in_shift_dr = (tap_state == 4'h4)`.
  - `in_run_idle = (tap_state == 4'h1)`.
- `rst_n` resets `tap_state <= 4'h0` (TEST_LOGIC_RESET).

#### Notes
Standardized JTAG TAP controllers provide boundary scan and on-chip CPU debug access.
solution_hints: Implement standard IEEE 1149.1 state transition table based on tms.
Assert in_run_idle in state 4'h1 and in_shift_dr in state 4'h4.
Reset to state 4'h0 on asynchronous rst_n.

title: Implement the timing: UART Frame Serializer with Parity Generation
description:
### Problem statement
A UART transmitter frames 8-bit data `tx_byte [7:0]` into serial output `tx_line` on posedge clk when triggered by `start_tx=1`:
1. START bit: `tx_line <= 0` (1 cycle).
2. DATA bits: 8 cycles transmitting `tx_byte[0]` through `tx_byte[7]` LSB first.
3. PARITY bit: if `parity_en=1`, transmit even parity bit `^tx_byte` (1 cycle).
4. STOP bit: `tx_line <= 1` (1 cycle).
Output `busy` asserts throughout transmission and deasserts when complete.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_uart_tx_parity(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start_tx,
    input  logic       parity_en,
    input  logic [7:0] tx_byte,
    output logic       tx_line,
    output logic       busy,
    output logic [3:0] bit_phase
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous transmission engine on posedge clk.
- When IDLE and `start_tx=1`: latch byte and parity mode, assert `busy <= 1, tx_line <= 0, bit_phase <= 0` (START bit).
- On successive clock cycles:
  - Phase 1..8: `tx_line <= latched_byte[phase-1]`.
  - Phase 9 (if `parity_en`): `tx_line <= ^latched_byte`.
  - Phase 9 (if `!parity_en`) or Phase 10 (if `parity_en`): STOP bit `tx_line <= 1`.
  - Terminal phase: `busy <= 0, bit_phase <= 0, tx_line <= 1`.
- `rst_n` sets `tx_line <= 1, busy <= 0, bit_phase <= 0`.

#### Notes
Correct parity and stop-bit framing ensures noise immunity across asynchronous serial cables.

    input  logic       rst_n,

Emit data bits LSB first across phases 1 through 8.
Emit even parity bit if enabled before driving stop bit high.

title: Checker: AXI-Stream TKEEP Contiguous Byte Enable Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In standard AXI4-Stream packet framing, null bytes are forbidden from appearing between valid data bytes within a packet beat. Specifically, once a byte lane has `tkeep[i] == 0`, all subsequent higher byte lanes in that beat must also be 0 (`tkeep[j] == 0` for all $j > i$). If an active keep bit appears after an inactive keep bit (sparse byte keep, e.g. `4'b1011` or `4'b0101`), an illegal sparse byte violation occurs. Output `err_sparse_keep` must assert high for 1 cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_axis_keep(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       tvalid,
    input  logic       tready,
    input  logic [3:0] tkeep,
    output logic       err_sparse_keep
);
```

#### Requirements
- Check on posedge clk during active handshakes (`tvalid && tready`).
- Violation condition: illegal patterns are `4'b0010`, `4'b0100`, `4'b0101`, `4'b0110`, `4'b1000`, `4'b1001`, `4'b1010`, `4'b1011`, `4'b1101`.
  - (Valid contiguous prefix patterns are only `4'b0000`, `4'b0001`, `4'b0011`, `4'b0111`, `4'b1111`).
- Output `err_sparse_keep <= (tvalid && tready && !is_valid_pattern)`.
- `rst_n` clears `err_sparse_keep` to 0.

#### Notes
Detecting sparse keep violations prevents illegal memory gaps in AXI-Stream packet processors.
solution_hints: Valid tkeep values must be contiguous lower-order ones: 0, 1, 3, 7, or 15.
Only evaluate during cycles where tvalid && tready handshake succeeds.
Register err_sparse_keep on posedge clk.

title: Checker: CDC Minimum Pulse Width and Sampling Aperture Guard
description:
### Problem statement
When crossing clock domains without handshake synchronization, a signal must maintain its asserted state for at least 2 destination clock cycles to guarantee reliable capture by a 2-flip-flop synchronizer. If `async_sig_in` pulses high for only 1 destination clock cycle (`pulse_width == 1`) and falls low on the very next cycle, a CDC pulse-eating hazard occurs. Output `err_too_narrow` must assert for 1 cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_cdc_edge_spacing(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic async_sig_in,
    output logic err_too_narrow,
    output logic [1:0] high_cycles
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `high_cycles` on posedge clk.
- When `async_sig_in=1`: increment `high_cycles <= (high_cycles < 3) ? high_cycles + 1 : high_cycles`.
- When `async_sig_in=0`:
  - If previous cycle had `high_cycles == 1`: `err_too_narrow <= 1`.
  - Else: `err_too_narrow <= 0`.
  - `high_cycles <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Narrow pulses crossing clock domains violate 1.5x destination period rules and can be swallowed silently.
solution_hints: Count cycles where async_sig_in stays high in high_cycles.
When signal falls, verify that high_cycles was at least 2.
Assert err_too_narrow if the pulse lasted only 1 cycle.

title: Reorder Buffer (ROB) In-Order Commit and Branch Squash Engine
description:
### Problem statement
In an out-of-order processor, instructions must commit in program order from the Reorder Buffer (ROB) head (`head_ptr [1:0]`). Entry at `head_ptr` has `ready` and `is_mispredict` status bits. If `head_ready=1` and `!is_mispredict`, the instruction retires successfully (`retire_val=1`), and `head_ptr` advances modulo 4. If `head_ready=1` and `is_mispredict=1`, a branch misprediction occurred: `retire_val=1`, and `squash_pipeline` pulses high to flush all speculative execution across the processor.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_rob_retire_head(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       head_ready,
    input  logic       head_mispredict,
    input  logic [1:0] head_tag,
    output logic       retire_val,
    output logic       squash_pipeline,
    output logic [1:0] retire_tag,
    output logic [1:0] cur_head
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2-bit pointer `head` on posedge clk.
- When `head_ready=1`:
  - `retire_val <= 1`.
  - `retire_tag <= head_tag`.
  - If `head_mispredict`: `squash_pipeline <= 1, head <= 0` (flush resets ROB head).
  - Else: `squash_pipeline <= 0, head <= head + 1`.
- When `head_ready=0`:
  - `retire_val <= 0, squash_pipeline <= 0`.
- Output `cur_head = head`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
ROB commit guarantees precise exception state despite out-of-order speculative execution.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       head_ready,
    input  logic       head_mispredict,
    input  logic [1:0] head_tag,
    output logic       retire_val,
    output logic       squash_pipeline,
    output logic [1:0] retire_tag,
    output logic [1:0] cur_head
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Advance head modulo 4 on successful instruction retirement.
Assert squash_pipeline when the retiring instruction is a mispredicted branch.
Reset head back to 0 on misprediction or reset.

title: Wear-Leveling Logical-to-Physical Block Translation Engine
description:
### Problem statement
A flash translation layer maintains a 4-entry mapping from Logical Block Address `lba [1:0]` to Physical Block Address `pba [1:0]`. When lookup occurs (`lookup_en=1`), `pba_out` combinationally returns the mapped physical block. When remap trigger occurs (`remap_en=1`), the table swaps mapping: `pba_table[lba]` receives `new_pba [1:0]` on posedge clk. Default initial mapping is identity: LBA 0->0, 1->1, 2->2, 3->3.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_wear_level_tbl(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       lookup_en,
    input  logic [1:0] lba_in,
    input  logic       remap_en,
    input  logic [1:0] remap_lba,
    input  logic [1:0] new_pba,
    output logic [1:0] pba_out,
    output logic       valid_map
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-entry table initialized to identity (0, 1, 2, 3) on reset.
- On posedge clk:
  - If `remap_en`: `table[remap_lba] <= new_pba`.
- Combinational outputs:
  - `pba_out = lookup_en ? table[lba_in] : 2'd0`.
  - `valid_map = lookup_en`.
- `rst_n` restores identity mapping.

#### Notes
Dynamic LBA-to-PBA remapping spreads write cycles evenly across all flash cells.

Update table[remap_lba] with new_pba when remap_en is asserted.
Read out table[lba_in] combinationally when lookup_en is high.

title: Four-Phase Level-Toggle Clock Domain Pulse Synchronizer
description:
### Problem statement
A pulse synchronizer transfers single-cycle pulses across clock domains. When input pulse `pulse_in=1` arrives in the source domain, the transmitter toggles an internal level register `tx_toggle <= ~tx_toggle` and asserts `busy=1`. The toggle passes through a 2-stage synchronizer (`sync1, sync2`). In the destination domain, an edge detector compares `sync2 != sync3` to generate output pulse `pulse_out=1`. When acknowledge toggle returns, `busy` deasserts, allowing the next pulse.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_pulse_sync_ack(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic pulse_in,
    output logic pulse_out,
    output logic busy,
    output logic tx_toggle
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous controller on posedge clk.
- On `pulse_in=1` when `!busy`: `tx_toggle <= ~tx_toggle, busy <= 1`.
- 3-stage shift synchronizer for edge detection: `s1 <= tx_toggle, s2 <= s1, s3 <= s2`.
- Output pulse: `pulse_out <= (s2 != s3)`.
- When `s3 == tx_toggle`: `busy <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Toggle-based pulse synchronization guarantees zero missed pulses across asynchronous domains.
solution_hints: Toggle tx_toggle when pulse_in arrives while not busy.
Pass toggle through shift registers s1, s2, and s3.
Generate pulse_out when s2 differs from s3.

title: PID Controller Anti-Windup Conditional Integral Clamping
description:
### Problem statement
In feedback control systems, integral windup occurs when physical actuator saturation prevents the control loop from closing, causing the error accumulator to build up excessively. An anti-windup clamping stage halts integration when actuator saturation is active (`saturated=1`) and the incoming error `err_in [7:0]` has the same sign as the saturated output. If `saturated=1` and `err_in > 0`, integration freezes. If `err_in <= 0`, integration resumes to pull the loop out of saturation.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_pid_anti_windup(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       enable,
    input  logic       saturated,
    input  logic [7:0] err_in,
    output logic [9:0] integral_acc,
    output logic       integrating
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 10-bit accumulator `integral_acc` on posedge clk.
- Conditional integration logic:
  - If `saturated && (err_in > 0)`: `integrating <= 0` (freeze accumulator).
  - Else if `enable`: `integrating <= 1, integral_acc <= integral_acc + {2'b00, err_in}`.
  - Else: `integrating <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears `integral_acc` and `integrating` to 0.

#### Notes
Anti-windup clamping eliminates large overshoots and settling oscillations in motor position control.

module sv_i_pid_anti_windup(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       enable,
    input  logic       saturated,
    input  logic [7:0] err_in,
    output logic [9:0] integral_acc,
    output logic       integrating
);
    // TODO: implement PID anti-windup conditional integration stage

endmodule
solution_hints: Check both saturated flag and the magnitude of err_in.
Freeze integral_acc when saturated and err_in is positive.
Accumulate err_in into integral_acc when enabled and not frozen.

title: Fix: Interleaved Memory Bank Read Grant Lockout Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A shared memory arbiter resolves read conflicts between CPU (`req_cpu`) and DMA (`req_dma`). In the default policy, CPU has priority over DMA. However, if CPU requests continuously for 3 consecutive cycles, DMA must be granted for 1 cycle to prevent starvation. In the flawed module, the counter failed to reset after granting DMA, causing DMA to be permanently locked out thereafter.

Fix the module so `cpu_burst_cnt` properly resets to 0 when DMA is serviced.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_sram_read_priority(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic req_cpu,
    input  logic req_dma,
    output logic grant_cpu,
    output logic grant_dma,
    output logic [1:0] cpu_burst_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2-bit counter `cpu_burst_cnt` on posedge clk.
- If `req_cpu && req_dma && (cpu_burst_cnt == 2'd3)`:
  - `grant_dma = 1, grant_cpu = 0`.
  - `cpu_burst_cnt <= 0`.
- Else if `req_cpu`:
  - `grant_cpu = 1, grant_dma = 0`.
  - `cpu_burst_cnt <= cpu_burst_cnt + 1`.
- Else if `req_dma`:
  - `grant_cpu = 0, grant_dma = 1`.
  - `cpu_burst_cnt <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Burst capping ensures DMA engines do not miss peripheral FIFO deadlines.
solution_hints: Check when cnt reaches 3 and both CPU and DMA are requesting.
Reset cnt to 0 on posedge clk when granting DMA.
Grant CPU normally when cnt is less than 3.

title: Fix: Carry-Save Adder Redundant Carry Alignment Bit Shift Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A 3:2 Carry-Save Adder (CSA) sums three 8-bit operands $A$, $B$, $C$. Full adder sum bits are $S_i = A_i \oplus B_i \oplus C_i$ and carry bits are $C_i = (A_i B_i) \vee (B_i C_i) \vee (A_i C_i)$. When passed to a downstream CPA, the carry vector must be shifted left by 1 bit (`carry_shifted = {c_vec[6:0], 1'b0}`) so that weights align. The buggy code failed to zero-pad LSB and dropped bit 7, shifting right instead.

Fix the module so `carry_out` correctly shifts the 7-bit carry left by 1 bit with LSB zero.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_fix_csa_sign_ext(
    input  logic [7:0] a,
    input  logic [7:0] b,
    input  logic [7:0] c,
    output logic [7:0] sum_out,
    output logic [7:0] carry_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- `sum_out = a ^ b ^ c`.
- Full adder carry bits: `c_gen = (a & b) | (b & c) | (a & c)`.
- Shifted carry: `carry_out = {c_gen[6:0], 1'b0}`.

#### Notes
Carry-save representation avoids carry propagation delay until the final vector merge stage.
solution_hints: Compute bitwise sum using 3-input XOR.
Compute bitwise carry-out using majority logic (a&b | b&c | a&c).
Left-shift the generated carry vector by 1 bit, zero-filling the LSB.

title: Implement the timing: Secure Digital (SD) Card Command-to-Response Timer
description:
### Problem statement
An SD host card interface transmits a 6-byte (48-bit) command packet on `cmd_line`, then waits between 2 and 8 cycles (Ncr turnaround delay) for the card response. During command phase (`cmd_phase=1`), `cmd_line` serializes `cmd_byte [7:0]` byte-by-byte (6 cycles total, 1 byte per cycle in this byte-clock model). Once all 6 bytes are emitted, the controller enters TURNAROUND wait state (`cmd_line` released high, `turnaround=1`). When response start bit arrives (`resp_start_bit=0`), `resp_phase` asserts.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_sd_cmd_resp(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic start_cmd,
    input  logic resp_start_bit,
    output logic cmd_phase,
    output logic turnaround,
    output logic resp_phase,
    output logic [2:0] byte_step
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous controller on posedge clk.
- When `start_cmd=1` from IDLE: `cmd_phase <= 1, byte_step <= 0, turnaround <= 0, resp_phase <= 0`.
- During `cmd_phase`:
  - Increment `byte_step <= byte_step + 1`.
  - When `byte_step == 5`: `cmd_phase <= 0, turnaround <= 1, byte_step <= 0`.
- During `turnaround`:
  - If `resp_start_bit == 0`: `turnaround <= 0, resp_phase <= 1`.
- `rst_n` resets to IDLE, all flags to 0.

#### Notes
Ncr turnaround timing compliance ensures host receivers do not sample intermediate bus float.

    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic start_cmd,

    output logic turnaround,
    output logic resp_phase,
    output logic [2:0] byte_step
);

endmodule

Enter turnaround wait state after byte 5 completes.
Assert resp_phase once resp_start_bit is pulled low by the card.

title: Implement the timing: SPI Mode 3 (CPOL=1, CPHA=1) Master Timing Engine
description:
### Problem statement
In SPI Mode 3, clock polarity is idle-high (`CPOL=1`) and phase is second-edge sample (`CPHA=1`). When active transfer begins (`cs_n=0`):
- SCLK falls on even sub-cycles (driving edge where MOSI changes).
- SCLK rises on odd sub-cycles (sampling edge where MISO is captured).
When `enable=1` and `cs_n=0`, output `sclk` toggles, starting from 1->0 on the first active edge.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_trace_spi_mode3(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic cs_n,
    input  logic enable,
    output logic sclk,
    output logic sample_edge,
    output logic drive_edge,
    output logic [3:0] edge_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- When `cs_n=1`: `sclk <= 1, sample_edge <= 0, drive_edge <= 0, edge_cnt <= 0`.
- When `cs_n=0 && enable`:
  - Increment `edge_cnt <= edge_cnt + 1`.
  - Toggle `sclk <= ~sclk`.
  - `drive_edge <= (sclk == 1)` (falling edge of SCLK).
  - `sample_edge <= (sclk == 0)` (rising edge of SCLK).
- `rst_n` sets `sclk <= 1`, all flags and count to 0.

#### Notes
SPI Mode 3 is widely used in high-speed flash memories and secure microcontrollers.

title: Checker: Shared System Bus Master Tenure Watchdog Timer
description:
### Problem statement
In multi-master on-chip interconnects, no single master may monopolize the shared bus longer than maximum tenure limit `tenure_limit [3:0]`. When bus grant `grant=1` is held while transfer active `busy=1`, an internal watchdog counter increments. If the counter reaches `tenure_limit`, a fatal bus lockout alarm `deadlock_alarm` pulses high, and `sticky_deadlock` latches high.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_bus_grant_watchdog(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       grant,
    input  logic       busy,
    input  logic [3:0] tenure_limit,
    output logic       deadlock_alarm,
    output logic       sticky_deadlock,
    output logic [3:0] held_cycles
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `held_cycles` on posedge clk.
- When `grant && busy`:
  - If `held_cycles == tenure_limit`: `deadlock_alarm <= 1, sticky_deadlock <= 1`.
  - Else: `deadlock_alarm <= 0, held_cycles <= held_cycles + 1`.
- When `!grant || !busy`: `held_cycles <= 0, deadlock_alarm <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all counters and alarm registers to 0.

#### Notes
Bus tenure watchdogs prevent rogue bus masters from freezing the entire SoC.

);

Assert deadlock_alarm when held_cycles equals tenure_limit.

title: Checker: Hardware Memory Allocator Double-Free Invariant Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
A hardware block allocator manages 4 memory chunks using an allocation bitmap `alloc_map [3:0]` (1: allocated, 0: free). When `alloc_req=1` with block ID `block_id [1:0]`, the block must be currently free (`alloc_map[block_id] == 0`); if already allocated, `err_double_alloc` asserts. When `free_req=1` with `block_id`, the block must be currently allocated (`alloc_map[block_id] == 1`); if already free, `err_double_free` asserts. Both violations latch sticky error flags.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_i_chk_mem_pool_double_free(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       alloc_req,
    input  logic       free_req,
    input  logic [1:0] block_id,
    output logic       err_double_alloc,
    output logic       err_double_free,
    output logic [3:0] alloc_bitmap
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-bit register `bitmap` on posedge clk, initialized to 4'b0000 on reset.
- On posedge clk:
  - If `alloc_req`:
    - If `bitmap[block_id] == 1`: `err_double_alloc <= 1`.
    - Else: `bitmap[block_id] <= 1, err_double_alloc <= 0`.
  - If `free_req`:
    - If `bitmap[block_id] == 0`: `err_double_free <= 1`.
    - Else: `bitmap[block_id] <= 0, err_double_free <= 0`.
  - If neither: `err_double_alloc <= 0, err_double_free <= 0`.
- Output `alloc_bitmap = bitmap`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Double-free detection protects hardware allocators against heap corruption vulnerabilities.

endmodule

Assert err_double_alloc if attempting to allocate an already set block.
Assert err_double_free if attempting to free an already clear block.
